summary: @qlik/tsconfig preinstall downloads Bun runtime to execute obfuscated bundled payload
details: The package presents itself as a static collection of TSConfig JSON files, but its package.json declares `"preinstall": "node setup.mjs"`. setup.mjs checks PATH for `bun`, and if absent downloads a Bun binary from https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v<ver>/<archive>.zip, extracts it to a temp directory, chmods it executable, and then execFileSyncs the sibling file `math_init.js` under that freshly-installed Bun runtime. `math_init.js` is a ~727KB single-line, heavily obfuscated bundle carrying the `// @bun @bun-cjs` marker, a rotating string-array decoder (WV8StW shifting entries of MmgoCP), a large opaque constant table (n7gIxM), and hex-mangled identifiers. Nothing else in the package references math_init.js; it exists solely to be executed by the dropped Bun runtime at install time. Neither setup.mjs nor math_init.js is listed in package.json's declared `files` array (which enumerates only node.json, react.json, recommended.json, strictest.json, vue.json), so the executable payload ships in the tarball outside the author-declared manifest — consistent with a compromised publisher token or malicious release under the @qlik scope. Installing this package runs attacker-controlled obfuscated code on the installer's machine via a non-Node runtime chosen to evade Node-based scanners.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
